content.text: Pope Joan is a quintessentially English historical card game that was immensely popular in the 18th and 19th centuries. A 'Stops' game played with a specialized rotating board, it blends sequence-building with 'Lucky Card' rewards. The game centers on the 'Pope Joan' cardâ€”the Nine of Diamondsâ€”which serves as a permanent wild card. It is a game of social interaction, anticipation, and the thrill of clearing a 'Stakes' board.
Dates back at least to the 1700s. It is named after the mythical female Pope Joan (the Nine of Diamonds), reflecting 18th-century anti-clerical humor.
Staking board with eight compartments (Ace, King, Queen, Jack, Game, Pope, Matrimony, Intrigue); counters or chips.
Deal the cards evenly, plus an extra hand (the 'Stop' hand) which remains face-down.

items.text: Standard stakes: Dealer places six counters in Pope, two each in Matrimony and Intrigue, one in each of Ace, King, Queen, Jack, Game.
Agreed counter value: Counter or chip value is agreed by the players before the game.
Split Matrimony or Intrigue: When King-Queen or Queen-Jack of trumps are in different hands, stakes in those compartments are sometimes divided.
